034/**
035 * Fluent builder for a single HTTP request.
036 *
037 * <p>
038 * Obtain instances from the {@link RestClient} factory methods (e.g. {@link RestClient#get(String)}).
039 *
040 * <p>
041 * <b>Beta — API subject to change:</b> This type is part of the next-generation REST client and HTTP stack
042 * ({@code org.apache.juneau.marshall.ng.*}).
043 * It is not API-frozen: binary- and source-incompatible changes may appear in the <b>next major</b> Juneau release
044 * (and possibly earlier).
045 *
046 * @since 9.2.1
047 */
048@SuppressWarnings({
049   "java:S1192", // Duplicate string literals are HTTP header names and REST protocol wire values; intentional
050   "resource"    // client is not owned here; run() transfers RestResponse ownership to caller
051})
052public final class RestRequest {
053
054   private final RestClient client;
055   private final String method;
056   private final String url;
057   private final List<HttpHeader> headers = l();
058   private final List<HttpPart> queryData = l();
059   private final List<HttpPart> formData = l();
060   private final Map<String,Object> pathData = m();
061   private HttpBody body;
062   private TransportBody convertedBody;
063   private boolean debug;
064   private URI resolvedUri;
065   private Duration timeout;
066   // Per-request interceptors, unioned with the client-level interceptors at run() time.
067   private final List<RestCallInterceptor> requestInterceptors = l();
068
069   RestRequest(RestClient client, String method, String url) {
070      this.client = client;
071      this.method = method;
072      this.url = url;
073      // Inherit client defaults
074      this.headers.addAll(client.defaultHeaders);
075      this.queryData.addAll(client.defaultQueryData);
076   }

082   /**

086    * @return This object.
087    */
088   public RestRequest headers(HttpHeader... value) {
089      headers.addAll(Arrays.asList(value));
090      return this;
091   }

093   /**
094    * Adds a request header.
095    *
096    * @param name The header name. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
097    * @param value The header value. May be <jk>null</jk> to omit.
098    * @return This object.
099    */
100   public RestRequest header(String name, String value) {
101      headers.add(HttpHeaderBean.of(name, value));
102      return this;
103   }
104
105   /**
106    * Adds a request header with a lazy value.
107    *
108    * @param name The header name. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
109    * @param value Supplier for the value. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
110    * @return This object.
111    */
112   public RestRequest header(String name, Supplier<String> value) {
113      headers.add(HttpHeaderBean.of(name, value));
114      return this;
115   }
116
117   /**
118    * Returns <jk>true</jk> if a header with the given name (case-insensitive) is already set on this request.
119    *
120    * <p>
121    * Used by the next-gen remote-proxy engine to honor the precedence of a caller-supplied
122    * {@code @Header} parameter over an annotation-declared {@code accept}/{@code contentType} attribute.
123    *
124    * @param name The header name. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
125    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the header is present.
126    */
127   public boolean hasHeader(String name) {
128      return headers.stream().anyMatch(h -> name.equalsIgnoreCase(h.getName()));
129   }

201   /**
202    * Adds path variable substitutions for URI templates (e.g. replaces {@code {id}} in the URL).

205    * @return This object.

207   public RestRequest pathData(HttpPart... value) {

228
229   /**
230    * Sets the request body directly from an {@link HttpBody}.
231    *
232    * @param value The body. May be <jk>null</jk>.
233    * @return This object.
234    */
235   public RestRequest body(HttpBody value) {
236      body = value;
237      convertedBody = null;
238      return this;
239   }
240
241   /**
242    * Sets the request body from an arbitrary Java object.
243    *
244    * <p>
245    * The object is first run through the client's body converter chain. The default converters handle:
246    * {@link HttpBody} (passthrough), {@link InputStream}, {@code byte[]}, and {@link File}.
247    * Custom converters can be registered on the builder.
248    *
249    * <p>
250    * If no converter matches, the object is serialized with the client's explicitly-configured default serializer
251    * ({@link RestClient#getDefaultSerializer()}) and sent as a string body using the serializer's content type.  When
252    * no default serializer is configured, an {@link IllegalStateException} is raised (there is no implicit JSON
253    * fallback) — configure one via {@link RestClient.Builder#defaultSerializer(org.apache.juneau.marshall.serializer.Serializer)}.
254    *
255    * @param value The body object. May be <jk>null</jk> to clear the body.
256    * @return This object.
257    * @throws IOException If a converter fails or the default serializer fails.
258    * @throws IllegalStateException If no converter matches and no default serializer is configured on the client.
259    */
260   public RestRequest body(Object value) throws IOException {
261      if (value == null) {
262         body = null;
263         convertedBody = null;
264         return this;
265      }
266      for (var converter : client.bodyConverters) {
267         if (converter.canConvert(value)) {
268            convertedBody = converter.convert(value);
269            body = null;
270            return this;
271         }
272      }
273      // No converter matched: stream the POJO through the client's default serializer.
274      // Mirrors classic SerializedEntity — the serializer writes straight to the transport output stream during
275      // run() rather than being pre-materialized into a String/byte[].  Repeatable (re-serializes on resend), so a
276      // future auto-retry can resend it; streaming bodies (InputStream/Reader) remain non-repeatable.
277      var s = client.getDefaultSerializer().orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalStateException(
278         "No default serializer is configured on the client.  Configure one via RestClient.Builder.defaultSerializer(...)."));
279      var mt = s.getResponseContentType();
280      body = SerializerBody.of(s, value, mt != null ? mt.toString() : "application/json");
281      convertedBody = null;
282      return this;
283   }
284
285   /**
286    * Sets the request body to a token/record-streaming cursor body.
287    *
288    * <p>
289    * Convenience for {@link #body(HttpBody) body(streamBody)} that documents streaming intent and avoids a cast.
290    * The {@link RecordStreamBody} writes directly to the transport output stream during {@link #run()}, so large
291    * payloads are streamed to the wire without being buffered in memory.
292    *
293    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
294    * <p class='bjava'>
295    *    <jv>client</jv>.post(<js>"/bulk-upload"</js>)
296    *       .streamBodyEntity(RecordStreamBody.<jsm>records</jsm>(<jv>w</jv> -&gt; {
297    *          <jk>for</jk> (Bean <jv>b</jv> : <jv>source</jv>())
298    *             <jv>w</jv>.write(<jv>b</jv>);
299    *       }))
300    *       .run();
301    * </p>
302    *
303    * @param value The streaming body. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
304    * @return This object.
305    */
306   public RestRequest streamBodyEntity(RecordStreamBody value) {
307      return body(value);
308   }
309
310   /**
311    * Sets the request body to a raw string (UTF-8, {@code text/plain}).
312    *
313    * <p>
314    * Unlike {@link #body(Object)}, this bypasses the converter chain and sends the string as-is.
315    *
316    * @param value The string body. May be <jk>null</jk> to clear the body.
317    * @return This object.
318    */
319   public RestRequest bodyString(String value) {
320      if (value == null) {
321         body = null;
322         convertedBody = null;
323      } else {
324         body = StringBody.of(value, "text/plain");
325         convertedBody = null;
326      }
327      return this;
328   }

348   // --------------------------------------------------
349   // Timeout / interceptors
350   // --------------------------------------------------
351
352   /**
353    * Sets a per-call response timeout for this request.
354    *
355    * <p>
356    * Threaded onto the {@link TransportRequest} and applied by the transport as the response/read timeout.  Connect
357    * timeouts remain a client-level setting.
358    *
359    * @param value The response timeout. May be <jk>null</jk> to use the transport default.
360    * @return This object.
361    */
362   public RestRequest timeout(Duration value) {
363      timeout = value;
364      return this;
365   }
366
367   /**
368    * Adds per-request lifecycle interceptors.
369    *
370    * <p>
371    * These are unioned with the client-level interceptors when the request runs: the client-level (builder)
372    * interceptors fire first, then these in the order added.  The next-gen remote-proxy engine uses this to layer
373    * annotation-declared interface-level then method-level interceptors after the builder-configured ones.
374    *
375    * @param value The interceptors to add. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
376    * @return This object.
377    */
378   public RestRequest interceptors(RestCallInterceptor... value) {
379      requestInterceptors.addAll(Arrays.asList(value));
380      return this;
381   }
382
383   /**
384    * Returns <jk>true</jk> if this request's body can be safely re-sent (retry gating).
385    *
386    * <p>
387    * A request with no body is trivially repeatable.  Otherwise the answer is delegated to the underlying
388    * body's {@link HttpBody#isRepeatable()} (or {@link TransportBody#isRepeatable()} for a pre-converted body):
389    * buffered bodies (string/byte[]/file/serialized POJO) are repeatable; one-shot streaming bodies
390    * ({@link InputStream}/{@link Reader}/piped) are not.
391    *
392    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the body is absent or repeatable.
393    */
394   public boolean isBodyRepeatable() {
395      if (convertedBody != null)
396         return convertedBody.isRepeatable();
397      if (body != null)
398         return body.isRepeatable();
399      return true;
400   }

424   // --------------------------------------------------
425   // Execute
426   // --------------------------------------------------
427
428   /**
429    * Executes the request and returns the response.
430    *
431    * <p>
432    * The caller is responsible for closing the returned {@link RestResponse}.
433    *
434    * @return The response. Never <jk>null</jk>.
435    * @throws TransportException If a network-level error occurs.
436    * @throws RestCallException If the response could not be processed.
437    */
438   @SuppressWarnings({
439      "java:S1130" // RestCallException retained for public-API/source stability: interceptors declare 'throws Exception', so a RestCallException they raise is caught by the precise-rethrow multi-catch below and propagated unchanged; Sonar's flow analysis misses this path. Removing the throws would break callers that catch RestCallException (a sibling checked exception of TransportException).
440   })
441   public RestResponse run() throws TransportException, RestCallException {
442      var start = Instant.now();
443      RestResponse response = null;
444      Throwable error = null;
445      // Union the client-level (builder) interceptors with any per-request (interface- then
446      // method-level) interceptors, preserving the order builder → interface → method.
447      var effectiveInterceptors = effectiveInterceptors();
448      try {
449         for (var interceptor : effectiveInterceptors)
450            interceptor.onInit(this);
451
452         var transportRequest = buildTransportRequest();
453         var transportResponse = client.transport.execute(transportRequest);
454         response = new RestResponse(transportResponse, client);
455
456         for (var interceptor : effectiveInterceptors)
457            interceptor.onConnect(this, response);
458
459         return response;
460      } catch (TransportException | RestCallException e) {
461         error = e;
462         throw e;
463      } catch (Exception e) {
464         error = e;
465         throw new TransportException("Request failed: " + e.getMessage(), e);
466      } finally {
467         var elapsed = Duration.between(start, Instant.now());
468         RestResponse finalResponse = response;
469         if (error != null && finalResponse != null) {
470            // The response was assigned but an error after that point (e.g. a throwing onConnect
471            // interceptor) means it is never returned to the caller, so the caller can never close it
472            // themselves — close it here to avoid leaking the underlying connection/body.
473            try {
474               finalResponse.close();
475            } catch (IOException closeError) { // HTT: close() failing on an already-broken response is not reliably reproducible
476               // suppress — best effort, and the original error is what propagates
477            }
478         }
479         for (var interceptor : effectiveInterceptors) {
480            try {
481               interceptor.onClose(this, finalResponse);
482            } catch (Exception e2) { // HTT: exception in onClose; hard to test reliably
483               // suppress interceptor close errors — best effort
484            }
485         }
486         if (client.logger != null) {
487            var entry = RestLogEntry.builder()
488               .request(this)
489               .response(finalResponse)
490               .error(error)
491               .elapsed(elapsed)
492               .debug(debug)
493               .build();
494            client.logger.log(entry);
495         }
496      }
497   }
498
499   /**
500    * Executes this request and opens a closeable, cancellable cursor over the response as a
501    * <c>text/event-stream</c>.
502    *
503    * <p>
504    * This executes {@link #run()}, asserts a 2xx response status, then opens the response body as an event stream.
505    * Non-2xx responses throw {@link RestCallException} before the body is treated as SSE.
506    *
507    * <p>
508    * The response content type is not validated. This is intentional so callers can branch on response type
509    * (for example <c>application/json</c> vs <c>text/event-stream</c>) when protocols use both.
510    *
511    * <p>
512    * Adds an {@code Accept: text/event-stream} header only when neither this request nor inherited client default
513    * headers already include {@code Accept}.
514    *
515    * <p>
516    * The caller owns the returned {@link SseEventReader}; closing it also closes the underlying
517    * {@link RestResponse} (see {@link ResponseBody#asEventStream()}). If opening the event stream fails,
518    * this method best-effort closes the response before propagating.
519    *
520    * @return A cursor over the live event stream. Never <jk>null</jk>.
521    * @throws IOException If a transport-level error occurs (typically {@link TransportException}), if the response
522    *    could not be processed (typically {@link RestCallException}), or if the response has no body to open a
523    *    stream over.
524    */
525   public SseEventReader openEventStream() throws IOException {
526      if (! hasHeader("Accept"))
527         header("Accept", "text/event-stream");
528      var res = run();
529      var opened = false;
530      try {
531         var r = res.assertOk().body().asEventStream();
532         opened = true;
533         return r;
534      } finally {
535         if (! opened)
536            quiet(res::close);
537      }
538   }
539
540   /** Returns the client-level interceptors followed by the per-request ones (builder → interface → method order). */
541   private List<RestCallInterceptor> effectiveInterceptors() {
542      if (requestInterceptors.isEmpty())
543         return client.interceptors;
544      var l = new ArrayList<RestCallInterceptor>(client.interceptors.size() + requestInterceptors.size());
545      l.addAll(client.interceptors);
546      l.addAll(requestInterceptors);
547      return l;
548   }
549
550   @SuppressWarnings({
551      "java:S3776" // Request-assembly branching is intentional and cohesive; refactoring would reduce readability without benefit.
552   })
553   private TransportRequest buildTransportRequest() {
554      var resolvedUrl = applyPathSubstitutions(url);
555      resolvedUri = appendQuery(resolvedUrl);
556
557      var builder = TransportRequest.builder()
558         .method(method)
559         .uri(resolvedUri)
560         .timeout(timeout);
561
562      // Headers
563      for (var h : headers) {
564         var v = h.getValue();
565         if (v != null)
566            builder.header(h.getName(), v);
567      }
568
569      if (client.parsers != null || client.defaultParser != null) {
570         var hasAccept = headers.stream().anyMatch(h -> "Accept".equalsIgnoreCase(h.getName()));
571         if (! hasAccept) {
572            var accept = client.getDefaultAccept();
573            if (accept != null)
574               builder.header("Accept", accept);
575         }
576      }
577
578      // A Content-Type already present in the header list (a caller-supplied @Header param, or a constant header)
579      // wins over the body's own content type, and is never duplicated by it (dedup invariant).
580      var hasContentType = hasHeader("Content-Type");
581
582      // Pre-converted body from body(Object) takes priority
583      if (convertedBody != null) {
584         if (convertedBody.getContentType() != null && ! hasContentType)
585            builder.header("Content-Type", convertedBody.getContentType());
586         builder.body(convertedBody);
587      } else if (!formData.isEmpty() && body == null) {
588         // Form body when form data is present and no explicit body was set
589         var formBody = buildFormBody();
590         if (! hasContentType)
591            builder.header("Content-Type", formBody.getContentType());
592         builder.body(TransportBody.of(formBody));
593      } else if (body != null) {
594         if (body.getContentType() != null && ! hasContentType)
595            builder.header("Content-Type", body.getContentType());
596         builder.body(TransportBody.of(body));
597      }
598
599      return builder.build();
600   }
601
602   private String applyPathSubstitutions(String template) {
603      var result = template;
604      Object remainder = null;
605      for (var entry : pathData.entrySet()) {
606         if ("/*".equals(entry.getKey())) {
607            remainder = entry.getValue();  // @PathRemainder — applied after named substitutions
608            continue;
609         }
610         var replacement = entry.getValue() != null ? entry.getValue().toString() : "";
611         result = result.replace("{" + entry.getKey() + "}", urlEncode(replacement));
612      }
613      if (remainder != null) {
614         var r = remainder.toString();
615         if (! r.isEmpty()) {
616            if (result.endsWith("/*"))
617               result = result.substring(0, result.length() - 2);
618            if (! result.endsWith("/"))
619               result += "/";
620            result += urlEncodePath(r);
621         }
622      }
623      return result;
624   }
625
626   /** URL-encodes a path remainder while preserving {@code /} segment separators. */
627   private static String urlEncodePath(String value) {
628      var segments = value.split("/", -1);
629      var sb = new StringBuilder();
630      for (var i = 0; i < segments.length; i++) {
631         if (i > 0)
632            sb.append('/');
633         sb.append(urlEncode(segments[i]));
634      }
635      return sb.toString();
636   }
637
638   private URI appendQuery(String baseUrl) {
639      if (queryData.isEmpty()) {
640         try {
641            return new URI(baseUrl);
642         } catch (URISyntaxException e) {
643            throw iaex(e, "Invalid URL: %s", baseUrl);
644         }
645      }
646      var sb = new StringBuilder(baseUrl);
647      var first = !baseUrl.contains("?");
648      for (var part : queryData) {
649         var v = part.getValue();
650         if (v == null)
651            continue;
652         sb.append(first ? '?' : '&');
653         sb.append(urlEncode(part.getName())).append('=').append(urlEncode(v));
654         first = false;
655      }
656      try {
657         return new URI(sb.toString());
658      } catch (URISyntaxException e) {
659         throw iaex(e, "Invalid URL: %s", sb);
660      }
661   }
662
663   private HttpBody buildFormBody() {
664      var sb = new StringBuilder();
665      var first = true;
666      for (var part : formData) {
667         var v = part.getValue();
668         if (v == null)
669            continue;
670         if (!first)
671            sb.append('&');
672         sb.append(urlEncode(part.getName())).append('=').append(urlEncode(v));
673         first = false;
674      }
675      final var encoded = sb.toString();
676      return new HttpBody() {
677         @Override public String getContentType() { return "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"; }
678         @Override public long getContentLength() { return encoded.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).length; }
679         @Override public void writeTo(OutputStream out) throws IOException { out.write(encoded.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)); }
680         @Override public boolean isRepeatable() { return true; }
681      };
682   }
683
684   private static String urlEncode(String value) {
685      return URLEncoder.encode(value, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
686   }
687}
